Vietnam Pizza?
Feb 2015 • Solo
I had a craving for pizza, so when I saw the sign, I thought I was in luck. But just to be sure, I flagged down the doorman at one of the large hotels a few doors down from the pizza place. 

I asked him if the pizza there was good. He said yes, and that it was famous in Da Nang. Great!

The lady came to take my order, and I wrote down the toppings I wanted on my pizza and gave it to her: onion, tomato, basil, olive, bell pepper, mushroom and ham. Basic.

What I got was: sausage, pepperoni, ham, olive and bell pepper.

I was too hungry to protest, and it did not seem the lady who took my order spoke English well. So I ate the pizza. 

It became obvious this was a frozen factory pizza, and not handmade. Although the taste was acceptable, I was just thinking about factory pizza production and how the corporations that produce such items use the cheapest ingredients, including GMO and the like.

Well, I guess you cannot expect to find "real" pizza in Vietnam, and if you do, it would be fortunate indeed.

Cost with a 25,000VND beer was 160,000VND.

I would not go back for pizza at this restaurant, and would not reccomend it to others.

Now, just a few shops south, I was surprised to get a better slice of pizza by chance. There is a bar called Bamboo Bar, and I was asking the young server if she knew where the best pizza in Da Nang was. She mentioned another place, but said that the pizza at Bamboo was very good. She even brought me a sample slice, which was so much better than the place reviewed above. 

The crust was thin and crisp and tasty. The toppings had fresh onion and chunks of fresh squid. I know, not typical topping, but in Asia, you often find "seafood pizza," and this worked just fine for me. 

I would recommend Bamboo Bar pizza, and would go back for their pizza. Staff speaks English, and much more friendly than the place reviewed above. Good music, albeit a bit on the loud side.

Tiger beer on tap 30,000 VND.
